title: Reading Drill — Studying wait times at a clinic — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Studying wait times at a clinic — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The clinic administrator had been asked to investigate patients seeing late arrivals called first in Hillswick. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on time from check-in to being called, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a six-week comparison, the team used anonymous arrival records at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because urgent cases might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward a display explaining the appointment order. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
